03 / MODELS

Which model checks which technology

The website and the terminal program use the same engine file and the same model numbers. You choose a technology or describe a problem; the mapping layer sends it to one of these models.

#Thermodynamic modelTechnologies and examplesWhat it checksRole
1Fixed-temperature reservoir cyclic heat engineInventor’s engine, Stirling engine, power plant with given source and sink temperaturesCarnot limit, First Law, SgenCore
2Finite hot stream + finite cold stream (work produced)Waste-heat engines, CL 202 Base (coffee from GPU waste heat)Exact limit with Sgen = 0; Teff shown for informationCore
3General steady control volumeTurbines, compressors, nozzles, pumps (h and s from tables)Mass, energy and entropy balancesCore
4Closed systemPiston-cylinder, sealed tank, cycles with several reservoirs, “all heat into work” claimsEnergy balance and Sgen = ΔS − ΣQ/TCore
5Property changes onlyΔh, Δs, effective temperature, phase-change temperature (used in CL 202 Modified)Calculation utility — no verdictUtility
6Unsupported / future domainRefrigerators and heat pumps, tidal, transient systemsFallback — “model required”Fallback
7Heat exchanger (no shaft work)Heat recovery, data-centre coolant, oil–water exchangerEnergy closure, Sgen, temperature cross, exergy destroyedCore
8Mechanical energy harvestingWalking generator (both input styles), pedalling, wind (Betz), hydro (ρgQH), no-input claimsOutput ≤ recoverable mechanical inputExtension
9Solar radiation conversionSolar panels and convertersPetela–Landsberg limitExtension
10Electrochemical conversionFuel cells (H2, methane, methanol, ethanol)−ΔG × reaction rateExtension

Models 1–7 are the core thermodynamic models of the M3 terminal program. Model 5 is a calculation utility and Model 6 a fallback. Models 8–10 are domain extensions for technologies that are not heat engines, so no Carnot temperature is invented for them.

04 / UNDERSTAND

How the tester decides

01

Read and map

The analyzer finds each quantity and its unit, decides its role from the surrounding words, and identifies the source, the sink and the claimed output.

02

Calculate the limit

The Python engine applies the selected model and checks energy or entropy balances when the data support them.

03

Interpret the verdict

Feasible means the available balances and applicable limit pass within the selected model. Contradictions are rejected. Undetermined inputs remain insufficient data. This is a thermodynamic assessment, not proof of engineering or economic viability.
